title: Tokenizer + runtime compatibility contract upkeep for fallback variants
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Goal: Maintain and evolve the cross-variant compatibility contract between tokenizers, context window handling, and runtime tooling to ensure safe automatic fallback during smart routing. Scope includes: 1) audit of tokenizer normalization/byte encoding edge cases for current fallback set, 2) explicit context-length and truncation semantics across variants, 3) tooling sanity checks (export/import of KV cache, prompt canonicalization, rollout gating), and 4) automation to detect regressions during model onboarding and releases. Motivation: recent incidents where fallbacks produced tokenization drift or truncated prompts when routed across regions caused subtle semantic regressions in customer outputs. This work reduces customer-visible regressions and enables more aggressive fallback policies for cost/latency.

Deliverables:
- Compatibility contract doc (single-page) that enumerates tokenizer normalization, special-token tables, context-length semantics, and KV cache shape expectations.
- Automated nightly compatibility checks that run a matrix of prompts across primary+fallback pairs and surface diffs.
- Tooling changes: extend kv-export verifier, add tokenizer-normalization unit tests, and add a runtime flag to enforce strict-compat mode in Canary.
- Rollout checklist and gating criteria for switching on new fallback policies.

Acceptance criteria:
- Contract doc reviewed and approved by Runtime, Model-Onboarding, and Console teams.
- Nightly job added to CI; failing pairs create an alert in Slack + create an issue with example diff.
- Canary pass: strict-compat flag enabled in canary for 48h with no degradation in quality alerts (quality defined as automated BLEU-like and token-level diff thresholds).

Implementation notes and trade-offs:
- We must balance strict compatibility enforcement (which could block rollouts and slow onboarding) versus permissive fallback that increases availability. Plan: start with non-blocking alerts for 2 sprints, then move to warning-only policy during step rollouts, and finally enable optional blocking for P0-rated models.
- Tokenizer normalization fixes may change model inputs slightly. For models where normalization changes outputs, we will consider shipping a small migration shim that performs the old normalization as a per-variant toggle while owners update downstream evaluations.
- KV cache shape checks are currently best-effort due to variant-specific internal formats; we will define a minimal portable schema for prefix/KV export to validate presence/length rather than byte-exact equality in phase 1.

Links and artifacts:
- Draft contract doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RT/Variant+Compatibility+Contract+Draft
- Nightly check PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/6842 (WIP)
- Example incident postmortem: https://docs.redwood.ai/incidents/2026-02-tokenizer-fallback-drift
- KV export verifier prototype: https://github.com/redwood-inference/tooling/tree/main/kv-verifier
